reason: The text contains multiple named characters who are portrayed as regular human beings. The twelve spies are specifically named (Shammua son of Zaccur, Shaphat son of Hori, Caleb son of Jephunneh, Igal son of Joseph, Hoshea son of Nun, Paltiel son of Raphu, Gaddiel son of Sodi, Gaddi son of Susi, Ammiel son of Gemalli, Sethur son of Michael, Nahbi son of Vophsi, and Geuel son of Machi). Additionally, Moses and Aaron are named central figures. These characters are explicitly described as 'men' (anashim) and are portrayed as mortal human beings with individual names, family lineages, and human limitations (fear, doubt, mortality). While some hold leadership positions, they are fundamentally regular people as opposed to divine or supernatural beings.
